# `lock-order-cycle`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports two functions that acquire the same pair of locks in opposite nested
orders.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Concurrent calls can each hold one lock while waiting for the other, producing a
deadlock.

## When it fires

Both acquisition orders must be visible and use the same receiver fields. Opaque
or indirect lock calls are not inferred.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

const Bank = struct {
    primary: std.Thread.Mutex = .{},
    secondary: std.Thread.Mutex = .{},

    fn forward(self: *Bank) void {
        self.primary.lock();
        defer self.primary.unlock();
        self.secondary.lock();
        defer self.secondary.unlock();
    }

    fn reverse(self: *Bank) void {
        self.secondary.lock();
        defer self.secondary.unlock();
        self.primary.lock();
        defer self.primary.unlock();
    }
};
```
